title: Moving in Piassa, Arada & the Historic Core: Narrow Streets & Heritage Buildings
excerpt: Piassa and Arada moves: tight lanes, limited truck staging, heritage apartments, and how professional movers load safely in old Addis.
content:
Historic core challenges

Piassa, Arat Kilo, and surrounding Arada streets were built for pedestrians and small vehicles—not 3-meter moving trucks. Corridor redevelopment has also shifted traffic patterns. Moves here succeed with small-truck staging, hand carries, and early coordination with neighbors and building owners.

What to expect

  • Truck may park one or two blocks away; crew uses trolleys and multiple trips.
  • Older wood floors and narrow stairwells—padding and disassembly are essential.
  • Shop-adjacent buildings may have restricted hours; avoid market peak if possible.
  • Corridor construction detours—verify route the week before move day.

Retail and mixed-use

Ground-floor shops moving with residential units need inventory lists and after-hours loading where mercato-adjacent traffic is heavy. We treat these as commercial-residential hybrid quotes.

Professional vs day labor

Cheap informal trucks struggle with insurance, stair technique, and time—narrow-core moves punish understaffing. Use a written quote and trained crew.

Staging and permits

Building owners sometimes require notice before furniture crosses shared courtyards. If your lane is one-way during daytime market hours, plan a split load: soft goods first in a smaller vehicle, then disassembled frames when the street opens. Police occasionally redirect trucks during events near the historic core—confirm the week before move day.

Cost drivers

Narrow-core jobs bill for crew hours and carry distance, not bedroom count alone. A studio on the third floor without elevator access can exceed a larger suburban condo on one level. Read DIY vs professional true cost before hiring day labor without blankets or liability.

Religious and fragile items

Households in the historic core often move icons, books, and heirlooms that need padded cartons and hand carry—not loose truck stacking. Mention these at booking so crew size and time reflect careful handling. See religious items guide for packing norms.

Routes out of the core

Loads leaving Piassa for Bole, CMC, or Jemo still cross congested junctions. Early starts beat market-hour stalls. Pair timing rules with our Addis Ketema guide when your origin or destination touches Mercato-adjacent streets.

Split-load tactic

When lanes close during market hours, soft goods in a smaller first trip and frames after shops close reduces day-of conflict—coordinate with shop owners courteously.
